holidays.name: National Clean Out Your Refrigerator Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to bravely facing the science experiments growing in the back of your fridge. Toss expired condiments, mystery leftovers, and that container of something you swore you'd eat.
holidays.origin: Launched in 1994 by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's Food Safety program and observed in the U.S. to encourage fridge cleanouts, ahead of Thanksgiving, and to make room for holiday food.
holidays.funFact: Many people keep condiments far past their prime; some jars of mustard and salad dressing have been found in fridges for years, outliving several appliances and even a few relationships.

holidays.name: National Raisin Bread Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the sweet, cinnamon-swirled loaf studded with chewy raisins. Toast it, slather it with butter, and settle the great debate over whether raisins belong in bread at all.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday, popularized by food-observance calendars as a tribute to this bakery staple.
holidays.funFact: Raisins are simply dried grapes, and California produces about 40 percent of the world's raisins, with most of them grown near Fresno.

holidays.name: National Bundt Day
holidays.description: A day for honoring the ring-shaped cake with the fancy fluted edges. Bakers everywhere dust off their Bundt pans to make a cake that looks impressive with almost no decorating effort.
holidays.origin: The Bundt pan was created in 1950 by H. David Dalquist of Nordic Ware in Minneapolis, after members of a Hadassah group asked for a pan like the German kugelhopf pan. The holiday is observed on November 15 each year as a fan-made celebration of the cake.
holidays.funFact: The Bundt pan was a flop at first, until a Tunnel of Fudge Bundt cake won second place in the 1966 Pillsbury Bake-Off, causing a flood of over 200,000 pan orders.

holidays.name: I Love to Write Day
holidays.description: A day for scribbling, typing, journaling, and penning poems, novels, letters, or grocery lists with flair. Everyone is invited to express themselves in writing.
holidays.origin: Created by John Riddle of Delaware, who founded it in 2002 to encourage writing among people of all ages and to promote literacy.
holidays.funFact: The founder's goal was for people to use the day for writing of any kind, and many schools and libraries now host writing contests and workshops to mark it.

holidays.name: Recycle Your Phone Day / America Recycles Day
holidays.description: A day for sending the pile of dead gadgets in your junk drawer to a better place. Dig out old phones and recycle them, and recycle everything else you can along the way.
holidays.origin: America Recycles Day was started by the nonprofit Keep America Beautiful in 1997 to encourage recycling nationwide, and it takes place every November 15. Recycling old electronics has become a popular way to take part.
holidays.funFact: A million recycled cell phones can recover roughly 35,000 pounds of copper, 772 pounds of silver, 75 pounds of gold, and 33 pounds of palladium.
